title: INSTITUTE FOR THE TRANSLATION OF KOREAN CLASSICS ACT
full_text:
INSTITUTE FOR THE TRANSLATION OF KOREAN CLASSICS ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to laying the foundation for Korean studies and to the succession and development of traditional culture by establishing the Institute for the Translation of Korean Classics to collect, organize, and translate classical documents and to comprehensively manage information on translations of classical documents. <Amended on July 7, 2026>

Article 2 (Definitions)
For the purposes of this Act, "classical documents" means documents, books, and other records of academic research value written before 1909 in Chinese characters, Hangeul, or other writing systems.

Article 3 (Legal Personality)
The Institute for the Translation of Korean Classics (hereinafter referred to as the "Institute") shall be a corporation.

Article 4 (Establishment)
(1) The Institute shall be established upon registration of its incorporation at the location of its principal office.
(2) The matters to be registered under paragraph (1) shall be as follows:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Location of the principal office;
4. Names and addresses of its officers;
5. Method of public notice.

Article 5 (Articles of Incorporation)
(1) The articles of incorporation of the Institute shall specify each of the following matters:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Location of the principal office;
4. Projects and their implementation;
5. Organization;
6. Operation of the board of directors;
7. Officers and employees;
8. Assets and accounting;
9. Amendment of the articles of incorporation;
10. Dissolution;
11. Public notices.
(2) To amend its articles of incorporation, the Institute shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Education. <Amended on February 29, 2008 and March 23, 2013>

Article 6 (Projects)
The Institute shall undertake the following projects: <Amended on July 7, 2026>
1. Collection, organization, and research of classical documents;
2. Compilation, translation, and dissemination of classical documents;
3. Training of personnel for the organization and translation of classical documents;
4. Services to the public concerning classical documents;
5. Domestic and international exchanges and cooperation concerning classical documents;
6. Integrated management of information on translations of classical documents;
7. Ancillary projects related to those under subparagraphs 1 through 6, as specified by the articles of incorporation.

Article 7 (Appointment of Officers, etc.)
(1) The Institute shall have no more than 15 directors, including one president, and no more than two auditors.
(2) The president shall be elected by the board of directors, subject to the approval of the Minister of Education. <Amended on February 29, 2008 and March 23, 2013>
(3) Matters necessary for appointing directors and auditors shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(4) Officers other than the president shall serve on a non-standing basis.
(5) The term of office of a director, including the president, shall be three years, and that of an auditor two years; each may be reappointed.

Article 8 (Duties of Officers)
(1) The president shall represent the Institute, exercise general supervision over its affairs, and direct and supervise its employees. <Amended on March 23, 2021>
(2) Directors shall attend meetings of the board of directors to deliberate and resolve important matters concerning the Institute's affairs.
(3) Auditors shall audit the affairs and accounts of the Institute.

Article 9 (Board of Directors)
(1) The Institute shall establish a board of directors to deliberate and resolve the following matters:
1. Business plans, budgets, and settlements of accounts;
2. Amendments to the articles of incorporation;
3. Election and appointment of officers;
4. Acquisition, management, and disposal of property;
5. Management, operation, and use of donations;
6. Matters falling within the powers of the board as prescribed by the articles of incorporation;
7. Other matters important to the operation of the Institute submitted for deliberation by the chairperson of the board or the president.
(2) The board of directors shall consist of directors, including the president.
(3) The chairperson of the board shall be elected by and from among the directors, shall convene meetings of the board, and shall preside over them: Provided, That if at least one third of the incumbent directors request a meeting, the chairperson shall convene it without delay.
(4) Unless the articles of incorporation provide otherwise, resolutions of the board shall be adopted with a majority of incumbent directors present and with the affirmative vote of a majority of those present. <Amended on March 23, 2021>
(5) An auditor may attend a meeting of the board and state opinions.
(6) Other matters necessary for operation of the board shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 10 (Administrative Organization and Employees)
(1) The Institute shall have such administrative organization and employees as are necessary to conduct its affairs, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(2) Employees of the Institute shall be appointed and dismissed by the president as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 11 (Classical Translation Committee)
(1) The Institute shall establish a Classical Translation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") to deliberate on projects under Article 6 and on the selection of documents for translation and the order of their priority.
(2) The chairperson of the Committee shall be the president of the Institute, and members shall be persons falling within any of the following categories: <Amended on February 29, 2008 and March 23, 2013>
1. Persons recommended by institutions involved in the collection, organization, or translation of classical documents;
2. Persons recommended by organizations that research classical documents;
3. Public officials belonging to the Ministry of Education who are designated by the Minister of Education.
(3) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Operating Funds)
The Institute shall operate with the following financial resources:
1. Contributions and subsidies from the State;
2. Donations;
3. Other income.

Article 13 (Contributions or Subsidies)
(1) The State may contribute or subsidize, within budgetary limits, expenses necessary for the projects and operations of the Institute.
(2) The Institute shall submit to the Minister of Education, no later than April 30 of each business year, its request for budgetary contributions for the following year, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on February 29, 2008; March 23, 2013; and March 23, 2021>

Article 14 (Gratuitous Lease, etc. of State Property)
Where necessary for the establishment and operation of the Institute, the State may, notwithstanding the State Property Act, transfer State property to the Institute, lease it without charge, or permit its gratuitous use and enjoyment, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Cooperation in Affairs, etc.)
(1) The Institute may request the inspection, copying, or lending of materials necessary for projects such as organizing, translating, and researching classical documents from the State, local governments, individuals, corporations, or organizations possessing such materials. Unless there are special circumstances, a person receiving such a request shall comply with it. <Amended on March 23, 2021>
(2) When requesting inspection or copying of materials under paragraph (1), the Institute shall pay fair consideration to persons other than the State and local governments.
(3) Any individual, corporation, institution, or organization that has carried out a translation project for classical documents with financial support from the State, a local government, or a public institution may provide the Institute with information on translations resulting from that project. <Newly inserted on July 7, 2026>

Article 16 (Requests for Secondment of Personnel, etc.)
(1) When particularly necessary to achieve its purposes and enhance expertise, the Institute may, following consultation with the Minister of Education, request the secondment of personnel from State agencies, local governments, educational institutions, research institutes, and research organizations (hereinafter referred to in this Article as "State agencies, etc."). <Amended on February 29, 2008 and March 23, 2013>
(2) The head of any State agency, etc. receiving a request under paragraph (1) may second employees of that agency to the Institute.
(3) A person seconded to the Institute under paragraph (2) shall be deemed to be serving in the person's original institution during the secondment and shall not suffer any disadvantage in personnel status, remuneration, or otherwise solely on the grounds of the secondment.

Article 17 (Fiscal Year)
The fiscal year of the Institute shall coincide with that of the Government.

Article 18 (Submission of Business Plans, etc.)
The Institute shall submit its business plan and budget for each fiscal year to the Minister of Education and obtain approval before the fiscal year begins. The same shall apply where the Institute intends to make any material change to an approved business plan or budget. <Amended on February 29, 2008; March 23, 2013; and March 23, 2021>

Article 19 (Reporting on Settlement of Accounts)
The Institute shall submit to the Minister of Education a statement of settlement of revenues and expenditures for each fiscal year, accompanied by a report on the implementation of projects during that year, no later than March 31 of the following year. <Amended on February 29, 2008; March 23, 2013; and March 23, 2021>

Article 20 (Duty to Maintain Confidentiality)
An officer or employee of the Institute, or a person who formerly held such a position, shall neither disclose secrets learned in the course of official duties nor use them for purposes unrelated to those duties.

Article 21 (Prohibition of Similar Names)
No person other than the Institute established under this Act may use the name "Institute for the Translation of Korean Classics" or any similar name.

Article 22 (Deemed Status as Public Officials for Application of Penal Provisions)
Officers and employees of the Institute shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying the penal provisions of Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Article 23 (Mutatis Mutandis Application of the Civil Act)
Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Institute.

Article 24 (Penal Provisions)
Any person who violates Article 20 shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than one year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Amended on May 29, 2016>

Article 25 (Administrative Fines)
(1) Any person who violates Article 21 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won. <Amended on August 20, 2019>
(2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Education as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on February 29, 2008 and March 23, 2013>
(3) Deleted. <March 23, 2013>
(4) Deleted. <March 23, 2013>
(5) Deleted. <March 23, 2013>

ADDENDA <Act No. 8579, August 3, 2007>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Preparatory Acts Following the Enforcement of This Act)
Preparatory acts necessary for establishing the Institute under this Act may be undertaken before this Act enters into force.

Article 3 (Preparations for Establishment)
(1) The Minister of Education and Human Resources Development shall organize an establishment preparatory committee (hereinafter referred to in this Article as the "Committee") to take charge of affairs relating to the establishment of the Institute.
(2) The Committee shall consist of no more than 10 establishment preparatory members, including one chairperson; the chairperson and members shall be commissioned by the Minister of Education and Human Resources Development.
(3) The president of the Institute at its establishment shall be appointed by the Minister of Education and Human Resources Development.
(4) The Committee shall prepare the articles of incorporation and obtain authorization from the Minister of Education and Human Resources Development before this Act enters into force.
(5) Upon obtaining authorization under paragraph (4), all members of the Committee shall jointly register the establishment of the Institute without delay and then transfer the relevant affairs to the president of the Institute.
(6) The State shall bear the expenses necessary for establishing the Institute.
(7) Members of the Committee shall be deemed released from their appointments upon completion of the transfer of affairs under paragraph (5).

Article 4 (Succession to Rights and Obligations, etc.)
(1) Upon the establishment of the Institute under this Act, the Foundation for the Promotion of National Culture, a foundation established under Article 32 of the Civil Act and existing when this Act enters into force (hereinafter referred to as the "Foundation for the Promotion of National Culture"), shall be deemed dissolved notwithstanding the provisions of the Civil Act on the dissolution and liquidation of corporations. The Institute shall succeed to all property, rights, and obligations of that foundation. In this case, references to the foundation in property registers and other public registers concerning such property, rights, and obligations shall be deemed references to the Institute.
(2) The value of property succeeded to by the Institute under paragraph (1) shall be the book value at the time of succession.

Article 5 (Transitional Measures Concerning Employees of the Foundation for the Promotion of National Culture)
Persons employed by the Foundation for the Promotion of National Culture dissolved under Article 4 of these Addenda when this Act enters into force shall be deemed employees of the Institute under this Act.
